reviews.content:
Facebook was once a platform where people could genuinely connect — a space to share thoughts, have meaningful conversations, and stay in touch with friends and family. Sadly, those days are long gone.

Today, Facebook feels more like a business machine than a social platform. What used to be a fun, open space has turned into a pay-to-reach model. Even if you post something thoughtful or important, your own friends won’t see it unless you pay. Instead of rewarding intelligent or informative content, Facebook prioritizes ads and shallow engagement. The company wants users to pay to be heard — even by people who already follow them.

One of the most frustrating things is how Facebook constantly moves or hides features. It’s as if the developers deliberately make it hard for users to navigate. A recent example: the video watch history has completely disappeared in the latest update. This basic feature — which helps people find videos they previously watched — is nowhere to be found.

Even worse, privacy settings and controls are buried or hidden. Trying to adjust settings like ad preferences or third-party data sharing is a confusing nightmare. The app feels designed to make you give up — to keep scrolling instead of taking control of your own experience.

And what has Facebook really become now? A nonstop stream of Reels, flipping through video after video. You waste time watching random clips until you’re tired enough to fall asleep. The platform is no longer a place to learn, engage with ideas, or connect meaningfully. It’s now built to consume your time and attention — not feed your mind or strengthen your relationships.

Yes, I still use it — mainly to stay in touch with a small circle of people. But honestly, it’s just a matter of time before I delete it altogether. Facebook has become an unhealthy environment. It controls what you see, what you read, and what you think about. The experience is no longer free — not in terms of money, and certainly not in terms of freedom.

This all happened because the company is obsessed with monetization, squeezing profit out of every move you make. The moment you open the app, you’re no longer the user — you’re the product.

I hope one day, more people wake up and we all migrate to better, healthier platforms that actually value users, not just their data.
reviews.title: Facebook Is Broken — And It’s Time to Let Go

I love Amazon for how easy they make it for authors to publish their books. Thanks to their platform, I’ve been able to realize my dreams—and I know many others have too.

As an artist, I’m often shopping for unique and individual items to incorporate into my work. One feature I would really love to see is a folder or grouping option within the “Save for Later” section of the shopping cart. I frequently need to source various materials for specific projects, but I don’t always want to purchase everything at once. Being able to organize saved items by project would make it much easier to find and purchase them when the time is right.

Aside from that, I’ve been very happy with the interface and how easy the app is to use

reviews.content: I decided to try out the Picsart Pro version for a year. So far I like the functionality and relative ease of use. The A.I features are fun and I am sure they will continue to improve over time. However, the one issue I have, and it is a big concern that will give me reservations about renewing my subscription, is the rather small size of the edited picture files. I have noticed that pictures that start out with a file resolution  of approx 3-4 MB gets bumped down to less than 1MB when I save it as a JPEG file (a little higher if I save it as a PNG file). I have my Picsart settings set at the highest resolution. This is a very big problem when you want to print a picture beyond a 4X6” format. This is the biggest disappointment with Picsart so far. In addition to the low resolution output, there are the constant ads - I purchased a subscription. I should NOT be seeing ads in the app! Also, the UI could be streamlined. Navigating the app can be cumbersome and way too busy.

reviews.content:
The adds are insane, they used to be somewhat reasonable, now it’s an add that you can skip, three seconds of video, and another add. It’s insane. The app runs into issues that either full on reset the app to when you first opened it, or outright crash, forcing you to restart the app. Sometimes it randomly decides you might be a bot so it tries to force you to log in. This is all on top of them allowing people to continue making content after breaking the TOS.

Edit: the ads are unbearable. Now it’s “skip this add into the next add”, when it shouldn’t work like that at all. With the practices YouTube uses you would think they weren’t making any money and were desperately trying to convince google and their shareholders that they were. Also not one single person has ever clicked on an add, I have never done so on purpose, but if I even graze my screen YouTube decides that I did click the add and want to go to the page. I don’t want to go to the page, I don’t want to see the adds, I hate that they do this while letting anyone advertise on their platform. Stop redirecting people without their consent. Add an option that puts some sort of “are you sure you want to go to this page?” instead of just assuming someone does and sending them to the page.

And now there are near ten second adds that you can’t skip. I know it’s nearing the holidays so it’s add season but come on. Who thought this was acceptable?

Ten and fifteen second adds, often two in a row, that you cannot skip. The user experience is becoming so unbearable I have become inclined to look into add blockers and how to get around google/youtube’s crusade against something that improves lives by preventing every waking second of an individual’s life about being advertised to.

Somehow every update just makes the user experience worse. I genuinely don’t understand any part of the thought process that gets them from one update to another aside from making more money. I guess they have stopped pretending to care about the users at all.

Even more 15 second unskippable ads. Unbelievable. And they run into a second ad when they used to just be an annoying 15 second thing. This is unbelievable. I despise the direction YouTube has gone. They need to get it together or a real competitor will come along and dethrone them fast. Everyone hates ads so just have less of them.

I would commend them on adding additional language audio tracks for videos if they didn’t automatically switch from English (the only language I’m fluent in) to another language seconds into a video I want to watch and then refuse to switch back to English. What are you doing YouTube? Why do you feel the need to push things to users when they are clearly not ready?

Ads ads ads. Do advertisers genuinely think anyone will buy something from them after seeing an ad on YouTube? I actively avoid the products I see because of how egregious the adds and amount of ads is. Get rid of half the ads and the app becomes infinitely more usable. We have reached a point where people that didn’t use ad blockers are starting to because of how garbage the YouTube experience has become, and that isn’t even getting into all the people who should have been permanently banned by now still roaming the platform. Looking at you Logan Paul.

Now if you pause your video you get an ad. Skip ahead using their skip tool? Ad. Skip the add you just got from skipping ahead? Ad. This is insane. They have made the app almost unusable. These money hungry monsters need to get taken down a peg. I wish there was any alternative I could use that wasn’t bad. I’m genuinely furious that it has gotten to this point where you can’t go 5 seconds without being advertised to as though that’s all that matters.

Endless glitches. You’d think that after years of making the site infinitely worse in favor of adds they’d at least care enough to fix the endless problems the platform has but no, that would require money and time that they refuse to use on anything relevant.

Ads on ads on ads. They dropped to an acceptable level, closer to what they were 5 or so years ago, and went right back to where they were two weeks ago, a level which I find completely unacceptable. But of corse why would they ever care. It would be too easy to dismiss any and all criticism when you are the only game in town and your entire goal is to make as much money as possible.

Disguising ads as videos too. Unbelievable. I hate this app. I only even use it to follow the yard podcast anymore but I’m getting to a point where I might just have to drop money on patreon so I can watch through that instead.

And now there are insufferable amounts of adds for casinos. I think it might actually be illegal in many places including where I am from to run adds for casinos, even the online apps. YouTube used to matter and be a place where things of value existed. Oh how the mighty have sank into depravity.
reviews.title: So many problems.

reviews.content:
I have been a tiktok user for years. I’ve never paid for promotions or ads.

I’ve had two accounts. All with fandom based content, relatively generalized audiences.

The one with my face got so many followers. I made relatively simple minded jokes, did some makeup, discussed funny stuff. Okay.

My art account? Barely any so far. I cannot post art videos because of recording equipment—and most of the art side of tiktok is simple zooming on good quality tablets and screens. Cool, so why do videos with slideshows automatically get less views? Less scrolling? Why aren’t people scrolling? TikTok already destroyed their own algorithm. People aren’t putting in effort anymore. And that’s just surface level.

Also of note: I can find a beautiful girl’s video of her simply being confident in herself as well, and see her comment section filled with hate, kept up, not reported. Fatphobia, I see a lot of racism, numerous amounts of religious slop from all sides. It’s terrible. I have never been more disgusted and at a loss for hope for people MY AGE than online. And yes, I realize this: it’s online. My following point:

But comments that me and others post trying to actually be kind and help people on here (ie: recently had a comment taken down for trying to figure out what’s wrong with someone health wise) decline FAST. After the update, I’ve never, and I mean NEVER had so many comments taken down. I’m fighting them daily. This is absolutely ridiculous.

So we’re allowed to be horrible people on this app, but any other instance of is a natural cry for help and attention seeking? Nice! Use Rednote guys. The community is still 10 times better. I have no other place to fish my art out since Tumblr is also terrible now, so maybe someone with more power will see this and actually do something. I never write reviews. I never write BAD reviews. I’m livid. Please support your artists.
reviews.title: This App Is On A Decline

Deeply disturbing” research exposes how easy it is for children to encounter inappropriate content and interact unsupervised with adults on the gaming platform Roblox.

It comes as parents shared their serious concerns about children experiencing addiction, seeing traumatising content and being approached by strangers on the hugely popular website and app.

Roblox acknowledges that children using the platform may be exposed to harmful content and “bad actors”. It says it is working hard to fix this, but that industry-wide collaboration and government intervention are needed.

Describing itself as “the ultimate virtual universe”, Roblox features millions of games and interactive environments, known collectively as “experiences”. Some of the content is developed by Roblox, but much of it is user-generated. In 2024, the platform had more than 85 million daily active users, an estimated 40% of whom are under 13.

While the company said it “deeply sympathised” with parents whose children came to harm on the platform, it said “tens of millions of people have a positive, enriching and safe experience on Roblox every day”.

I hope this message finds you well.

We, as a group of concerned users, are writing to respectfully request the correction of a geographic naming error in your map service. The body of water currently labeled as the “Arabian Gulf” has been historically and internationally recognized as the Persian Gulf for over two millennia.

The name “Persian Gulf” is not only rooted in ancient historical records, such as those of Herodotus, Ptolemy, and countless Islamic and Western sources, but is also officially recognized by the United Nations and almost all international organizations and atlases, including the National Geographic Society and Encyclopædia Britannica.

Using alternative names undermines historical accuracy and can contribute to cultural and political tension. We respectfully urge you to uphold academic integrity and international standards by correcting the name on Google Maps to “Persian Gulf”.Thank you for your attention to this matter and for your commitment to providing accurate and responsible geographical information.

Sincerely

I have had an account for over ten years. It has been with me through deaths, my pregnancy, graduations, my engagement, my wedding and everything else. For us to be required to pay because of money hungry people is so disappointing. If we lose our memories due to payment I will be having wordsleaving. One it’s not legal 👉 Bottom line: If you didn’t agree to pay for old photos when you uploaded them, Snapchat can’t legally force you to now. They can only offer new paid services and ask you to opt in.

Paid features vs. access: Companies can introduce optional paid features (like enhanced storage, editing tools, or expanded access), but they cannot suddenly lock you out of your old content and demand payment unless you knowingly agreed to those terms.

Retroactive charges: They can’t legally go back and say, “We’re charging you now for photos you uploaded years ago,” unless the agreement at the time already allowed for it.

I have been playing Roblox for over 6 years now, and I’ve noticed that, things have changed (a lot!), let me explain my story. So I played Roblox so much when I first got it. I was obsessed. And the thing is, Roblox doesn’t do anything about it, which really frustrates me! If you haven’t noticed, Roblox now has, e-daters,and just a lot of inappropriate stuff in general. It has gotten really bad! Like I said, Roblox was never like this. And sometimes, when you chat, people can say some really bad things! Especially Voice Chat, that is a mistake. Considering this is a “Family Friendly Game”, I don’t think Voice Chat was the most brightest idea. Now, let me talk about the experiences.

The games in Roblox are very cool, like DOORS, Pressure, and etc, etc. But if you search up Sus (alternative word for suspicious), you’ll find the most inappropriate stuff you will probably ever see. Roblox is really not as Family Friendly as it used to be. Parents that are reading this review, if your little kid wants Roblox, please do not get it for them! There might be some things that you may not want them to see. In my opinion, this game is for 13+ ages. And I know, I’m not the only one who noticed this. For a little kid, I do not recommend, Roblox is more for mature audiences.

reviews.content:
Dear Snapchat Team,

It’s honestly cruel that you would delete the memories we’ve made and saved for years. These aren’t just random photos or videos — they’re personal moments, milestones, and pieces of our lives that we trusted your platform to keep safe. Many of us have been loyal users since day one, and to see those memories threatened is beyond disappointing.

What’s even worse is that you’re making us pay to keep them. Forcing people to buy access to their own memories is not only ignorant, but incredibly inconsiderate. You’ve built a platform centered around sharing and saving moments, and now you’re putting a price tag on the very thing that made Snapchat special in the first place.

This move shows a lack of empathy for the users who helped build your app into what it is today. It’s a crucial mistake that could cause a massive loss of trust, loyalty, and ultimately, users. Memories are personal and irreplaceable — once they’re gone, they’re gone forever.

Please reconsider this decision. People shouldn’t have to pay to keep their own memories alive.

Sincerely,

reviews.content:
Vista Mundo was a soul bathing experience, unplugging on my terms. Surrounded by nature’s mountainous greenscape, butterflies, dragonflies, and birds of stunning beauty, you can’t help but feel a connection with the world at a slower pace in a way you’ve never felt before.

I was here to escape from the pressures of life for some me time, and to finish writing my next book. I could not have picked a more perfect place! The hospitality from the welcome to the community potluck was fabulous. It is a place to disconnect and make connections in profound ways. 

Since I love to cook, the fully equipped kitchen was fabulous for me being inspired from the massive farmers market selections as one of my excursions, with everything you can imagine. A foodies’ paradise if you also love to entertain and cook.

I reveled in the two nearby guided waterfall hikes, and enjoyed relaxing by the infinity pool with perfect temperatures to enjoy fully. 

If you’re looking to get away from it all, and don’t want a tourist trap, Vista Mundo is your destination. 

I will be back! And bringing others to experience this unique and wonderful place.
reviews.title: A great escape

reviews.content:
I left Uber for five primary reasons, culminating in a complete loss of trust in the platform.

Firstly, I was the target of a scam by a driver named Xing. While I was in the car, he falsely claimed there was a problem with my credit card and insisted I cancel the ride. I later realized this was a scheme for him to collect a cancellation fee of approximately five dollars without having to complete the trip or use any gas. Even after this, he attempted to coerce me into requesting another ride so he could repeat the scam. This essentially functioned as an "infinite money glitch" for dishonest drivers; for example, had he succeeded in making me cancel ten times, he would have fraudulently earned about fifty dollars. I must give credit where it's due: Uber did eventually refund the fee after I reported the incident.

Secondly, my confidence was further shaken when I received an email from Uber stating my account had experienced an unauthorized security breach. While the email assured me my bank account was "safe," this was incredibly difficult to believe after the previous scam.

Thirdly, on a separate occasion, the app suddenly and without warning logged me out of my account. I was completely unable to access the service to get to work that day. This direct failure cost me multiple hours of wages, similar to the first incident. This was the final straw that pushed me to start using Lyft exclusively from that day forward.

Fourth, when I attempted to seek help for these issues, I found Uber's customer service to be utterly inaccessible. There was no option to call them directly for immediate assistance.

Fifth, my only recourse was the web-based support, which was severely delayed in its response. When they finally replied, they accused my account of recently violating community standards. This was both baffling and insulting. How did I violate the standards? By being defrauded by one of their drivers? Or by having my account compromised in a security breach that could have led to identity theft or a bank account hack? This was especially alarming for a platform that handles highly sensitive data, including social security numbers.
reviews.title: Why I Deleted Uber: A Story of Scams, Security Issues, and Poor Support

reviews.content:
The app has had issues for a while now. A few of the big ones are: notification issues, screen tilt issues, and 2-step verification issues. 
For a long while now, if you don’t allow your phone notifications from the app you won’t be notified of anything (the bell icon won’t let you know the status of a comment). I think this may be a larger YouTube issue because it extends to the browser as well. As for the screen tilt, if I am watching a video horizontally and an ad comes up, the perspective will be messed up when the video starts again. It will shrink in size with additional black boxes around the border, and you have to physically pick up your phone to fix it, sometimes it takes several tries. And 2-step verification. When you log into a new computer and are asked to verify via the app on your phone, you cannot already have the YouTube app open or the notification will disappear. If you tap the notification while the app is open it will direct you to the Home Page instead of to the Yes/No verification. You must close the app completely and ask for the notification to be send again. These issues have been going on for nearly a year now and it’s sad to see they haven’t been fixed.

reviews.content:
I’ve been using CapCut Mobile for a very long time now, and I absolutely love it. It’s been my go-to editing app for years. It’s fast, reliable, and packed with features that make editing on the go super convenient.🔥

However, there’s one feature I feel is really missing — a search bar for imported audio files (like background music and sound effects). Right now, when I import music into CapCut, it stays saved in the “Extracted” section, which is great. But over time, as I import more and more tracks, it becomes hard to scroll through everything just to find one specific file.😭

As someone who edits regularly and reuses a lot of background music, being able to search by name would save me a lot of time and frustration. This small feature could make a huge difference in workflow efficiency for many users like me.

The PC version of CapCut already feels more optimized in some areas, and this is one of them. I really hope the team can consider adding a search function for imported media in the mobile version too. It would take an already amazing app to the next level!🔥

Thank you, CapCut team — keep up the great work! 🔥❤️

reviews.content:
The X app is unnecessarily draining system resources on my iPhone 16 Pro Max, even when not actively in use. It’s sending data in the background for unclear reasons, leading to significant battery drain, overheating, and system slowdowns. Other apps also begin to malfunction, freezing or crashing as a result of the strain. Both my iOS and the X app are fully up-to-date, and my iPhone has almost all memory free. There’s no transparency on what data is being used or why. This issue is affecting my device’s performance, and it’s concerning that it continues to be allowed on the App Store. Please investigate and fix these issues to ensure the app follows proper performance and transparency standards.

It’s frustrating to see the App Store allowing Twitter to flood the comments section with obvious bot-generated 5-star reviews. There’s clear evidence that these reviews are being artificially boosted, likely through Twitter’s own AI systems, which can generate fake feedback. This undermines the integrity of the review system and misleads users who are trying to make informed decisions. It’s concerning that Apple’s marketplace is enabling this behavior, and I urge Apple to take action against fake reviews to ensure genuine user experiences are accurately represented.
reviews.title: X app drains resources and causes overheating

reviews.content:
I’ve been a longtime music lover, but I can no longer justify supporting Spotify. Their treatment of artists is appalling — the compensation rates are so low that even well-known musicians struggle to earn a fair income from streams. For independent artists, it’s essentially exploitative, with Spotify reaping massive profits while creators get scraps.

On top of that, the company’s moral compass seems completely broken. Spotify has run ads and partnerships that align with extremist and fascist agendas, which is unacceptable for a platform that claims to support creativity and culture. Even worse, they’ve been linked to investments in AI projects connected to weapons development. Using revenue from music listeners to fund tools of violence is about as far as you can get from the values of community, art, and humanity that music should represent.

There are better alternatives out there for music streaming — platforms that pay artists more fairly and don’t funnel money into harmful industries. I can’t in good conscience continue to support Spotify, and I encourage others to think twice before giving them your money
reviews.title: Spotify Falls Short on Fairness to Artists and Responsibility to Listeners

reviews.content:
I am writing to express my strong concern about the removal of the order archive feature from customer accounts. This change has significantly impacted my ability to use Amazon services comfortably and has resulted in reduced usage of the platform.

The Problem:
Without the ability to archive orders, my complete purchase history is immediately visible whenever | open the Amazon app or website. This creates serious privacy concerns when using Amazon around family members, friends, or in any shared space. I can no longer browse Amazon casually or make purchases when others might see my screen.
Impact on My Shopping 

Experience:
• I now avoid using Amazon when others are present
• My overall Amazon usage has decreased significantly
• I feel uncomfortable accessing my account in most situations
• Simple tasks like checking order status or browsing products have become anxiety-inducing

Request:
I respectfully request that Amazon restore the order archive feature or implement an alternative privacy solution that allows customers to control the visibility of their purchase history. Many customers relied on this feature for legitimate privacy reasons, and its removal has created a significant user experience issue.
This privacy concern affects my willingness to continue as a regular Amazon customer. I hope Amazon will reconsider this policy change and prioritize customer privacy
reviews.title:
Request to Restore Order Archive Feature -
Significant Privacy Impact

Dear Google Maps Team,

I hope this message finds you well.

We, as a group of concerned users, are writing to respectfully request the correction of a geographic naming error in your map service. The body of water currently labeled as the “Arabian Gulf” has been historically and internationally recognized as the Persian Gulf for over two millennia.

The name “Persian Gulf” is not only rooted in ancient historical records, such as those of Herodotus, Ptolemy, and countless Islamic and Western sources, but is also officially recognized by the United Nations and almost all international organizations and atlases, including the National Geographic Society and Encyclopædia Britannica.

Using alternative names undermines historical accuracy and can contribute to cultural and political tension. We respectfully urge you to uphold academic integrity and international standards by correcting the name on Google Maps to “Persian Gulf”.Thank you for your attention to this matter and for your commitment to providing accurate and responsible geographical information.

Sincerely

reviews.content:
I am absolutely appalled by the terrible customer service I’ve received from Roblox regarding my 7-year-old son’s hacked premium account. As a paying customer who has dutifully forked over $9.99 every month for a premium membership, I expected at least a modicum of support and professionalism. Instead, I’ve been met with nothing but incompetence, indifference, and what feels like a complete disregard for my concerns.

When my son lost access to his account, clearly hacked, I immediately reached out to Roblox for assistance. What followed was an endless cycle of frustration. Instead of helping me regain access or reset the password, I’ve been subjected to a barrage of canned, robotic responses that have done nothing to resolve the issue. Despite the account being linked to my email address, I’ve been repeatedly told to create a new email address. How is that even a solution? It’s not my email that’s the problem— it’s your system’s failure to secure my son’s account!

To make matters worse, when I attempt to reset the password, the account no longer shows up as connected to my email. This is a glaring security flaw that Roblox seems unwilling to address. Instead of taking responsibility, they’ve effectively shrugged their shoulders and suggested I start over.

And now, after weeks of back-and-forth, I’m being told that they may not reimburse me for the premium membership fees I’ve paid, nor will they cancel the subscription. This is nothing short of a scam. I’m paying for a service I can’t access, and Roblox’s response is to essentially say, “Tough luck.”

It’s painfully obvious that Roblox’s customer service is either entirely bot-driven or staffed by individuals who lack the authority or willingness to actually help. There’s no empathy, no problem-solving, and no accountability. As a parent, I’m not just frustrated - I’m furious. My son is heartbroken over losing his account, and Roblox’s inability to resolve this issue is adding insult to injury.

Roblox, you need to do better. Your paying customers deserve real support, not robotic runarounds. If this is how you treat loyal users, it’s no wonder so many people are losing faith in your platform. I was banned from Snapchat despite using it strictly for personal reasons and never violating any of their policies. I feel I was unfairly targeted. I’ve been a loyal Snapchat user for years, using the platform to stay connected with friends and family. Many people I know use Snapchat for the same harmless reasons — sharing moments from daily life, like I did with my puppies and the occasional outdoor selfie.

I did submit an appeal, but unfortunately, I never reached anyone who could help. This all happened earlier this year, right around the time Snapchat rolled out their AI systems. Ironically, I still see plenty of inappropriate content circulating on the platform, yet I was banned without ever posting anything questionable myself.

I used to love Snapchat — but for some reason, I’ve been cut off, and I still don’t understand why.

reviews.content: Instagram needs to seriously rethink how it handles banning people’s accounts. Too many users are getting permanently removed without clear explanations or warnings. One minute everything is fine, and the next, you're locked out — sometimes for vague reasons like "violating community guidelines," even when no harmful content was posted. The process feels automated and unfair, and it leaves creators, small businesses, and everyday users without a way to defend themselves. What makes it worse is the lack of communication and transparency. Instagram doesn’t give people a real chance to appeal or explain their side. Their help system is slow, unhelpful, and often leads nowhere. It’s frustrating and disheartening when you’ve spent years building a community, only to have it taken away with no proper explanation or support. A platform this big should treat its users with more respect and accountability. Banning should be a last resort, not a first reaction. There needs to be a better review system that involves real human oversight and clearer guidelines. Instagram is supposed to be a space for connection, creativity, and free expression — but right now, it feels like they’re more interested in control than fairness. If this continues, more and more people will start looking for better, more trustworthy platforms. i hatee ts they need to update and upgrade they support!
reviews.title: disabled accounts for no reason

reviews.content:
Update: several years later and still NONE of these issues have been resolved. 

Overall, the app is quite good. However, there is still lots of room for improvement. 

 1) Offline translate, isn’t. Download and install French and it still requires internet access to translate even common words. 

 2) Real-time translate is absolutely useless. Any very slight movement of the camera causes changes in results making true translation impossible. Image import is far more useful. 

 3) Definitions for translated words are given in the original language with no option to then copy/paste the definition to understand what it says.

4) Real time speech translate is useless. It is far too slow to keep up with even a slow speech pattern and then times out after only a short period of time. Any spoken words are then lost to the wind in the time required to restart the translation process.
reviews.title: Good but still needs bug fixes

reviews.content: YouTube is a well known app that allows individuals to post and watch videos from across the globe.  The infrastructure to perform such a task must be incredible, however as the app has aged it has begun to become actively hostile to its users. Most of it is small things, such as being unable to minimize a video if an ad is playing, to the search functionality steadily growing worse.  More still however is that ads have become rampant as Google continues to make more and more decisions to rampantly advertise everything on the platform.  Not only this, ads are more intrusive than ever and often times contain ads that are falsely advertising or are sometimes straight up suggestive/pornographic.   It is filled with bugs and incomplete features, for example the community tab is still broken on many devices despite years of promises that it was coming, and the app purposefully resets itself when you turn your device off then on, forcing you to find what you were watching, and sit through more ads to get back to where you were.  I can’t give a good review to an application that tries as hard as it can to make itself worse to try to squeeze more money out of the people.
reviews.title: A once great platform steadily brought down

Start - I've played this game since maybe 2018. This game has so many fun options to play, and you can play with your friends. You could communicate using typing only. There is also a sort of currency for extra things, but you don't need it. 

New - Lately, they created a “voice chat” option. This allows you to communicate using your actual voice. You have to get it approved using a phone number first though. 

Safety - Older adults are now using this game as a online dating app, so make sure your kids are set under the age limit so they can't join those games. However, people still join regular games and do dirty things. You can put blocks on specific people only when they join that specific game you are in. Make sure to report them if something happens. 

HOWEVER - I love Roblox so much, but I worry about parents letting their kids on here, not knowing what goes on. This game is great for long-distance friends and making friends. But please be careful!

reviews.content:
Google Maps has made an astonishingly unsafe design choice by forcing drivers to answer on-screen pop-up questions about road conditions while actively driving. These pop-ups last for 30 seconds, taking up valuable screen space and blocking crucial navigation information until the driver physically interacts with the device—forcing them to take their hands off the wheel.

This is beyond irresponsible. It is outright dangerous. Distracted driving is one of the leading causes of accidents, and yet Google has intentionally designed a feature that demands driver interaction in the middle of driving, disregarding every fundamental principle of road safety. This is not just a bad user experience—it is a direct threat to public safety.

Google should be held legally accountable for implementing a feature that actively endangers drivers and passengers. This design could easily lead to accidents, injuries, or fatalities. As such, I will be reporting this to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) and the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) for review under regulations concerning driver distraction and unsafe UI/UX design in vehicle-use applications.

Google, remove this feature immediately before you find yourself facing a class-action lawsuit. You are knowingly endangering lives for the sake of crowdsourced data, and that is unacceptable.
reviews.title: A Dangerously Irresponsible Design

Listen, I love Pinterest as much as the next guy, I use it daily— and have been for many, many years. I use it for personal projects such as inspiration creative writing, photo collaging, and references for art! However; there are of course. things I think that’s really dragging the app down, particularly the use of AI, and the addition of advertisements.  

Firstly, this app is supposed to be inspiration; mainly for people who do creative projects. I’ve seen many of the reviews complain of the use of AI in the app and I agree! Contrary to popular belief, and what big consumers/companies want everyone to think, many people do not want it! This is a DIY, creative space, and AI is not DIY OR creative. It is generative slop taken from other REAL people’s work. I could go on about this but I don’t want to be anymore long winded than I already am being. 

I don’t need an advertisement every five seconds, and while I understand the art of promotion and even have one or two boards that are purely products; it’s getting to the point where even I can’t find gifs or photos of actual inspiration, art or people unless I dig through advertisement after advertisement. 

So in a very long winded rant; remove the AI and cut back on the adds; bring back the actual artistry of the app!!!!!!!!!!!

reviews.content:
Hi,

I absolutely hate this new update. It’s genuinely one of the worst changes I’ve seen on this app. Everything that used to make Instagram easy and enjoyable has been messed up for no reason.

First off, removing the feature where you could slide left to go to the profile that made the reel? Horrible decision. That was my favorite feature — I used it constantly. Ever since it’s been removed, I still catch myself sliding left out of habit… and every single time, I just sit there and cry a little inside. Whoever decided to remove that clearly doesn’t actually use the app like real people do.

Then there’s the story like button. Why on earth would you move it from the right side to the left? My right thumb does all the work — liking, commenting, sharing — it was smooth and natural. Now I have to awkwardly switch hands just to leave a like, and honestly, I don’t even bother anymore. My thumb still automatically goes to the right side, and every time I end up opening the comment section instead, I get more irritated. It’s just bad design, plain and simple.

And the messages being moved to the bottom? Terrible idea. It was perfectly fine at the top. Now I keep looking for it where it should be, and it completely ruins the flow. Seeing reels my friends send is more annoying than ever — it’s like you’re intentionally making things harder for no reason.

The only semi-decent part is being able to swipe between sections, but even that could be better. The order is weird — messages should be second and “For You” should be third. If you want people to use Instagram to message more, maybe make it easier to reach instead of burying it.

This update feels like change for the sake of change — not improvement. It’s clunky, frustrating, and honestly just sad to see the app go backwards like this. Please, undo these awful changes and bring back the features that actually made sense.

I don’t remember who their partners are the names of their children, whether their mother died last month. In part is because I have some communication disorders. But probably more influential is the fact that I am on the autism spectrum. And Facebook has helped me pull together a very large portion of my Social Network, keeping Network Entropy “at bay”  as it were. Now, the old medieval (Norman)  French “aboi” or “Bay” referred to the barking of a pack of hunting dogs are scaring their quarry, a deer or a boar, when  cornering them. The cornered animal, or unwelcome stranger, would be kept at a distance by the barks “guarded aux abois” which in English became “kept abay” then “kept at bay”. Who is doing the barking? My friends from long ago, whose names I’ve forgotten, the exact relationship of which has fallen away from my busy mind? No. Prior to my engagement with Facebook the barking dogs were set loose daily  on myself by myself. Barking at myself for not engaging socially properly which I ascribe to a combination of three different communication disorders and of course Autism - Yet another failure in my long unendingly accumulating list of shortfalls which I can keep up with correcting or retraining. But I am proud to say that social networking has not been my personal error-as-a-human sheet since 2009 when I joined Facebook (Fb). Fb helped me get back in touch with classmates, friends, and colleagues, long lost cousins and aunts and uncles whom I had neglected to honor for way too long, business associates and academic acquaintances with “aplomb”. That’s another interesting word from the old French “a plumb” which carries the meanings of both ‘composure’ and ‘perpendicularity’ or literally ‘according to the plummet’. Fb scaffolded a way for me to engage the opaque world of social relationships via means I could grasp and grok and play with and build associations and not just cope but soar. Thank you Fb. reviews.content:
Great for research and creative tasks, but verify sources

I’ve been using this app extensively for creating images, diving deep into product evaluations, and exploring medical topics. It’s fast and intuitive once you get the hang of how to prompt it effectively—definitely a learning curve, but worth it.

The main drawback is that when you ask for references, especially scholarly sources, it can sometimes generate fake citations with made-up authors or publications. So, it’s important to double-check the information and not rely on it blindly.

That said, it’s still miles ahead of Gemini in terms of usefulness—Gemini felt like a waste of both time and money. Overall, this app has become a go-to tool in my workflow.

(I wrote this review on my own and the had this app rewrite it.)

I’ll start off by saying that I don’t normally write reviews. I hope my voice is not alone, and that the developers address the issues.
I’ve had this app for years. One of the best features is the “Audio Extraction” feature. It is now a premium feature. A few years ago, it was not. Rather than develop more intriguing features with the intention for them to be premium exclusive, the Devs have opted to take away a previously free feature. 
I would like to ask that this decision be reversed. CapCut is renowned for being user friendly and BUDGET friendly- and they have essentially “locked” one of their most appealing products from the general public. I don’t believe more people will pay for premium; people don’t want to pay for things they already had. We’re going to find alternatives. Believe me, it was super disappointing to log in and try to download a project, only to realize I’m unable to without paying $24 bucks a month (or $220 a year). I would’ve considered paying for better, more interesting features; however, forcing users to pay for essential services, knowing the app’s reputation, is just a bad look. 

I implore the developers to reconsider. Thank you.

reviews.content:
Unfortunately, using CapCut has become a disappointing experience for many Arab women and other users around the world due to the clear violation of privacy regarding personal photos and videos. It is completely unacceptable to impose mandatory conditions that force users to agree to the use of their personal content for the company’s own purposes.

We pay real money to subscribe to this app’s services, and it makes no sense that we are also required to “pay” with our privacy by allowing the use of our personal media without clear, respectful consent.

Many users have already chosen to delete the app, and if this policy continues, CapCut will undoubtedly lose a large segment of its loyal community.

Privacy is a basic right. It’s not fair to pressure users to choose between either giving up their privacy or abandoning the app entirely.

We sincerely hope you reconsider these practices and respect the users who helped make CapCut one of the leading editing apps globally.

reviews.content:
Spotify is a great app whether you have premium or whether you don’t. You can listen to millions of songs and podcasts for free! The app is easy to use and is somewhat customizable. 
Cons of non-premium:
1. There is an add either before every song or every other song
2. You cannot choose your add preferences. Eg. you can’t decide that you would rather not hear horror movie ads when around kids. 
3. You cannot customize your homepage so that you do not see inappropriate album covers, ect. 
4. You only have 5 skips and hour, plus you cannot play specific songs, it cycles through a few before it actually plays the one you want. 
5. Every playlist is on shuffle and you cannot download music. Podcasts are still downloadable.

Pros of non-premium: 
1. You don’t have to pay for the app.
2. All the same songs/podcasts are right at your fingertips.

Cons of premium:
1. It’s a little pricey, but once you’re on, your whole family can be on for the price of one, which is awesome.
2. you still cannot customize your homepage page so that you don’t see stuff that you don’t like in your feed.
3. I wish the app was a little bit more customizable. I think it would be fun if you could change the color theme of the entire app and the icon of the app. ( premium and non-premium still are very customizable such as changing your profile photo and playlist covers)

Pros of premium:
1. There are no ads. ( need I say more?)
2. You can download music so you can listen to it offline.
3. You have the option to shuffle your playlists if you would like, but it is not permanently stuck on it. 
4. You have unlimited skips!


Overall Spotify is a great app for listening to music, but if you are a parent thinking about letting your kids get it, I believe it would be wise to monitor what they listen to and what they are seeing in the app, because it’s not always very kid-friendly. But overall, I’m loving it. I hope this is helpful to someone!
reviews.title: Premium and non-premium

I’m incredibly disappointed with the latest Instagram update for iPad. The previous layout was perfect, clear, intuitive, and easy to navigate. This new version, however, is a nightmare. Everything feels long, cluttered, and scattered. The home page, Reels, DMs, profiles. Nothing is easy to use anymore. Navigation is frustrating, and it’s hard to focus on anything when everything is disorganized.

DMs are especially bad now. Messages are hard to follow, and keeping track of conversations is exhausting. What used to be a smooth, enjoyable experience has become stressful and confusing. I honestly don’t understand why this change was needed, the old layout worked perfectly.

This update has made the app feel more like a chore than a fun, social experience. It’s so frustrating and overwhelming that I’m seriously considering quitting Instagram altogether until this is fixed. At the very least, there should be an option to switch between the new and old layouts.

Instagram, please listen to your users. The iPad experience has gone from enjoyable to irritating, and this update is pushing people away rather than keeping them engaged.

I’ve been a loyal Roblox player, but this recent experience has completely ruined my trust in the platform. I was wrongfully banned due to a situation that was clearly a setup—and Roblox’s moderation system handled it poorly.

I was playing Grow a Garden and having a normal chat about trading pets. Then, another player suddenly asked me, “What’s the English of mataba?” (mataba means “fat” in my native language). I simply gave the correct answer—“fat.” That’s it. It wasn’t an insult or meant to hurt anyone. The rest of the conversation was completely innocent and game-related.

To my shock, I got banned shortly after. It’s obvious I was baited into saying something that could be taken out of context, and instead of protecting me—the victim—Roblox chose to punish me. It feels like they didn’t even review the full chat history before making a decision. If they had, they’d see that there was nothing inappropriate in the exchange.

Because of this unfair ban, I missed an important in-game event that I had been looking forward to. It was really upsetting and frustrating. I tried to appeal, but it feels like no one is really listening or taking the time to understand what actually happened.

Roblox, your moderation system seriously needs improvement. You ban innocent players without context, while actual rule-breakers often slip through. Players should not be penalized for honest answers or simple misunderstandings—especially when they are clearly being set up.

This entire experience has been deeply disappointing. I expected better from a platform that claims to support creativity, fairness, and community. Until real changes are made to moderation and how reports are handled, I can’t give this app anything more than one star.

reviews.content:
Roblox has become one of the most popular gaming platforms in the world, with millions of active users daily. It offers players the chance to create their own worlds, interact with others, and experience a wide range of user-generated games. While the platform has undoubtedly revolutionized gaming and provided a creative outlet for many, it also has a dark side. The community has been criticized for its toxicity, with many users facing harassment, bullying, and exposure to inappropriate content. Furthermore, there is a growing concern about child predators taking advantage of the platform’s largely unregulated social features. Given the platform’s widespread appeal, especially to younger audiences, it’s important to acknowledge the dangers and advocate for improvements to make Roblox a safer, more fair environment for all its users.

Toxicity in the Roblox Community

One of the most significant issues on Roblox is the prevalence of toxic behavior. The platform’s vast social network and the ability for players to interact in real-time can foster positive interactions, but it can also create a breeding ground for cyberbullying. Many young users have reported being targeted by other players, receiving hurtful comments, or being excluded based on their in-game behavior. Toxicity can often stem from the anonymity the platform offers, allowing users to hide behind usernames and avoid real-world consequences for their actions.

A major issue lies in how harassment is sometimes normalized within the community. Toxic language, including racist, sexist, and other harmful comments, is often found in group chats, comments, and even within games themselves. Although Roblox has implemented chat filters, these systems can be easily bypassed by malicious players, and not all forms of toxicity are adequately addressed. As a result, many young players experience distress and anxiety, and it can lead to a negative experience for those trying to enjoy the game in a safe and friendly environment.

The Threat of Child Predators

In addition to the toxic behavior prevalent in Roblox, there is a significant concern regarding child predators. The platform, which is primarily designed for children, allows users to create profiles, chat with others, and engage in online multiplayer games. While Roblox has established parental controls and content moderation tools, they are not foolproof. Predators can exploit the platform’s lack of comprehensive monitoring and find ways to contact children, making the environment unsafe for young users.

The platform’s social features, such as in-game chat and messaging systems, open up the possibility for predators to groom young players, manipulate them emotionally, or even attempt to meet in person. Roblox’s policy of permitting users to customize their avatars and create their own games also opens the door for inappropriate content, including sexually explicit material or disturbing behavior. Despite Roblox’s efforts to block inappropriate content and monitor the platform, the sheer scale of the platform, combined with its rapid growth, makes it difficult to fully eliminate these threats. As a result, many children are exposed to risks that their parents might not be aware of.

The Unfairness of Roblox’s Moderation and Reporting Systems

Another problem contributing to the toxic atmosphere on Roblox is the fairness, or lack thereof, in its moderation and reporting systems. Many users have criticized the way Roblox handles complaints and enforces rules. Some players have reported being banned unfairly or having their accounts suspended for minor infractions, while others are allowed to engage in harmful behavior without facing consequences. This inconsistency breeds frustration and a sense of injustice among players, especially when it feels like harmful individuals are not being held accountable for their actions.

For instance, Roblox has a system where players can report others for violating the platform’s rules, but these reports are often not adequately investigated. Many players feel that the moderation team’s response is slow or ineffective. This can lead to a sense of helplessness among those who experience harassment or abuse, as they may feel that reporting the issue won’t lead to meaningful consequences for the perpetrator. Furthermore, Roblox’s automated systems sometimes fail to detect inappropriate content or behavior, leaving players to deal with harmful situations on their own.

Recommendations for Improvement

To address the issues of toxicity and child safety, several improvements can be made to Roblox’s platform:
	1.	Enhanced Moderation Systems: Roblox needs to invest in more advanced moderation tools, such as AI-powered content monitoring, to ensure that toxic and inappropriate behavior is identified and addressed more efficiently. A team of human moderators should also be more involved in investigating reports, particularly those involving child predators or serious harassment.
	2.	Better Reporting Features: The reporting system should be more accessible and transparent. Players should receive clear feedback about their reports, including whether actions have been taken against offending users. This would help to restore trust in the platform’s safety measures and give players a greater sense of empowerment.
	3.	Stronger Privacy Controls: Roblox should provide more robust privacy settings for younger users. This could include features like default privacy settings that restrict communication to only friends or family, and stronger limitations on who can contact or message players. It would also be beneficial to implement more strict verification for accounts to ensure that players under the age of 13 are not easily contacted by strangers.
	4.	Parental Controls and Education: Roblox should continue to improve its parental controls and educate parents about how to monitor their children’s online activities. Giving parents the tools to set appropriate restrict

reviews.content: Roblox is an exceptionally valuable platform because it integrates creativity, education, and entertainment, rendering it accessible and enriching for individuals of virtually all ages. Distinct from conventional video games, Roblox functions as both an immersive gaming environment and a sophisticated creation tool, enabling users to design original experiences, cultivate programming and design competencies, and channel their imagination into interactive digital spaces. Younger players benefit from engaging with safe, developmentally appropriate activities, while older users are able to pursue more complex endeavors such as advanced game design, collaborative innovation, and entrepreneurial opportunities within the platform’s expansive marketplace. Moreover, the immense diversity of experiences—ranging from narrative-driven adventures and strategic simulations to social and role-playing communities—ensures that Roblox appeals to a wide spectrum of interests and cognitive styles. By fostering critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration, Roblox transcends the boundaries of mere entertainment and establishes itself as a multidimensional platform that supports both intellectual growth and personal development across age groups.

I DID actually press “gift” but for whatever reason it gifted it to ME. Now, I’m never going to use this weapon, power, whatever, so I call Roblox and leave a message, also wrote an email. “Please complete the transaction and gift this thing to little Jimmy, he keeps asking me for it.” MANY days later, I get a follow up email from Roblox asking for all the details: what card I used, who I am, copies of receipts, who the recipient is, code names, etc.  endless data sets they NEED to figure this out appropriately. The fact that Roblox is allegedly threatening legal action against someone trying to expose harmful behavior sends the wrong message. If the platform is truly committed to being a safe, family-friendly space, it should welcome community efforts to protect kids—not silence them.

reviews.content:
Cannot turn off ai! Don't want it, don't need it, adds nothing to my experience, wastes enormous amounts of energy and water completely unprompted for no reason -e.g. I just searched for an account and it gave me a summary of the brand--I don't need a summary and didn't ask for it.  I already knew what the brand was when I typed the name. Now that is a waste of energy I absolutely never needed and don't want to be responsible generating that with every search.  The ai info is creepy and the data collection is creepy.  This should be an OPT IN feature. At least give us the option to turn it off.


Other concerns:

As someone who always has all push notifications (and most internal ones) disabled, I was not aware that my followers could get push notifications about my like and comment activity on posts from other accounts.  This is extremely disturbing to me.  Obviously, I know it they see a post I liked, they may see my name beneath it, but I was not aware that their phone could like up with a pop up notification saying "__ just liked this post." Apparently, even though I have a private account, I cannot prevent my follower from getting a push notification that I commented on someone else's post.  PLEASE allow users to prevent other people from getting push notifications from their activity.  This is extremely creepy and an invasion of privacy.  If you do not enable the ability to turn this off, I will stop "engaging." I do not intend to ever post a comment again and will massively scale back my likes.
reviews.title: Let us Opt OUT of AI "features"

I am getting really tired of the algy not doing a better job. It’s not a cheap ‘premium’ service, but it’s not offering a premium experience. There could very easily be a setting to put lists of things I am very or mildly interested in, and things I absolutely do not want recommended- even if for some reason, such as work or study, I have needed to view something I am not interested in.

reviews.content: I’m giving Snapchat 1 star because this update has absolutely ruined the app. Snapchat used to be a place where we could store memories, chats, and streaks without worrying that they’d disappear, and now they’ve decided to make us pay for storage and only give us 12 months before everything gets deleted. That completely destroys what made Snapchat different and special in the first place. Most people used the app because it was fun, stress-free, and reliable — now it just feels greedy and manipulative. Why should we have to pay to keep our own memories? It’s frustrating and unfair, especially when so many of us have years of photos and videos saved there. Instead of rewarding loyal users, Snapchat is punishing us by holding our memories hostage unless we subscribe. The app has gone from being a fun social platform to something that feels like a cash grab, and honestly, it’s pushing me (and a lot of other people) to stop using it altogether. Snapchat should be listening to its community, not driving them away with paywalls and unnecessary changes.

reviews.content:
I’ve been a loyal Snapchat user for years, and like many others, the main reason I’ve stayed on this app is because of Memories. Snapchat isn’t just about quick snaps; it’s about storing and looking back on those moments, big and small, that make up our lives. It’s one of the only social platforms that gave us the gift of saving memories without worrying about storage limits on our phones.
Now, Snapchat has introduced a policy where we’re expected to pay for Memories if they go over 5GB. This is not just disappointing, it feels wrong. The entire point of Memories is to keep our most important moments safe. For many of us, these aren’t just random selfies or throwaway photos. They are deeply personal memories. In my case, I have Memories of passed loved ones, who tragically passed away. I cannot risk losing those, and I know I am not alone. Many people rely on Snapchat as the only place where their most meaningful moments still live.
Having a subscription for fun extras, filters, or exclusive features makes sense. That’s optional. But charging people to hold on to their most precious memories; the very foundation of why Snapchat is still relevant; feels exploitative. Snapchat should be protecting the emotional trust people have placed in them, not monetizing it.
The truth is, many users keep Snapchat purely because of Memories. To suddenly put those memories behind a paywall feels like betraying the community. Our memories are priceless, and taking them hostage for a subscription fee is unfair.
I really hope Snapchat reconsiders this decision. Memories should remain what they were always meant to be: a safe, free place where users can return to the moments that matter most.
reviews.title: Don’t hold our memories hostage

reviews.content:
This might sound chronically online enough to anyone who reads this, but it’s a bit of a slap to the face when an app that platforms art and inspiration decides it wants to shamelessly shill ai moderators and bot posts that put its entire existence to shame. 

I’ve been a few years-strong user, and I’ve saved THOUSANDS of pins. I have (or HAD) carefully organised boards for my interests and hyperfixations, like mythology, aesthetics, worldbuilding, etc. Not one board contained anything genuinely nsfw, “exploitative” or otherwise alarming, not ONE. Yet due to an issue I’ve heard from so many others in the same boat as I, that is the wildly inaccurate “moderation” of Pinterest’s automated system, I’ve lost my account. 

I got sent the first ban email, and I appealed it thinking well, it’s just a mistake. What did I get in return? A permanent suspension for appealing. The emails never ever listed a reason, example, or anything, they were all the same cookie cutter bot responses. 

Is this how you treat your user base who have proven themselves loyal enough that they’d continuously appeal to you? I know you’re trying to make it sound like we’re the ones that actually broke the rules, but it’s not. There’s a whole forum of people who have been banned in the past months as a result of this wave of incompetency. People are now backing up their accounts and moving elsewhere because you (as a team or whatever) don’t care enough to manually review these mistakes and god forbid APOLOGISE. 

I have sent 13 appeals, always palmed off to a bot that slaps me with even more suspension emails, like oh wow I never know! Thanks for reminding me! 

And my amount of appeals don’t even compare to others I’ve seen, and no, they never broke a single rule either. Tell me why I used to see so much pornographic material that never got so much as CENSORED, but my mythology board with Greek statues is likely what got me blacklisted off the god damn app? It’s the only thing I can think of, this is disgusting. 

Also everybody is noticing the quality dropping after these “updates” because there’s more ai trash and advertisement than ever before from what I’ve seen on friends’ unbanned accounts.

Fix your mistakes.
reviews.title: Mass banning & ai

reviews.content:
In terms of bedding ideas getting perspectives and doing basic research it’s like two or three research assistances. Absolutely amazing. Although there’s probably some room for improvement in terms of streamlining information back into one’s ecosystem. That said the integration with Obsidian is excellent.

HOWEVER it doesn’t think for you. You can’t trust the details of what it delivered back to you. If you don’t know the content area, you are on risky ground if you rely on it for anything substantive. I have discovered many mistakes along the way, thankfully there are things that jump out at me. And we have a discussion around things. It tends to work very well.

Certainly suggest using it as though you were having a conversation with somebody. The scaffolding of the AI within the conversation is amazing. 

Finally, I will say that it will be useful for the company to have some very thorough tutorials on the limits of what can be done. I think that has been missing, or it has not been obvious to me. Perhaps the most challenging thing is making sure that you lock in key concepts in terms. Even when you do that data information with flow back to you. So you always have to be on your game. If you treat it with the same degree of basic trust, but not absolute certainty that you would extend to a research assistant then you probably would have realistic expectations.

reviews.content: Persian Gulf, shallow marginal sea of the Indian Ocean that lies between the Arabian Peninsula and southwestern Iran. The sea has an area of about 93,000 square miles (241,000 square km). Its length is some 615 miles (990 km), and its width varies from a maximum of about 210 miles (340 km) to a minimum of 35 miles (55 km) in the Strait of Hormuz. It is bordered on the north, northeast, and east by Iran; on the southeast and south by part of Oman and by the United Arab Emirates; on the southwest and west by Qatar, Bahrain, and Saudi Arabia; and on the northwest by Kuwait and Iraq. The term Persian Gulf sometimes is employed to refer not only to the Persian Gulf proper but also to its outlets, the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf of Oman, which open into the Arabian Sea. This discussion, however, focuses primarily on the Persian Gulf proper.

reviews.content: As you all know, Roblox is a game where you can explore it's millions of games made by other players and also make your own! The game itself is one of the most popular games in the world and is loved by every single one of it's players. I personally love this game for it's range of games which always keep me entertained. But, eventually, you run out of fun games to play, get tired and lose interest in your favourite games and start to feel like Roblox isn't fun anymore. Searching for games on YouTube doesn't help, asking friends doesn't help and you eventually get sick of it! I have personally experienced this feeling before and started to watch Netflix and YouTube more often and tell myself to not waste my time on Roblox. But, the perfect solution is to just take a break! A break would make you forget about what you've experienced! That would be the perfect time to join back and experience an entire platform of fun and enjoyment! The feeling of joining back is what makes me love Roblox so much! I have loved Roblox since I was six so I believe anyone can love Roblox as much as I do! And that wraps it up! Thank you for reaching this point of my review! I hope you can love Roblox as much as I do! Goodbye!

reviews.content:
Dear OpenAI Support Team,

I am writing to express serious concerns about the privacy practices within the Sora platform, which I accessed through a paid subscription to your services. I have discovered that content I created using Sora — including images that draw on original ideas and cultural content — was made publicly available by default, without clear and informed consent from me as the user.

This occurred despite the fact that I am a paying subscriber, and I reasonably expected basic privacy standards and protections to be in place. At no point during the content creation process was I clearly informed that my work would be automatically published to a public “Explore” feed or accessible via direct URL links.

This default exposure has caused me distress, harm to my creative integrity, and a deep breach of trust, especially considering that some of my original work has been used or remixed by others without my consent.

I am formally requesting:
	1.	That all of my previously created content be fully deleted, including any copies or backups stored on your servers or accessible via URLs
	2.	That OpenAI commit to changing the default setting for all users — especially paying users — so that content is private by default
	3.	That you issue a refund for the duration of my paid use of Sora, as I did not consent to these conditions and was not provided with clear or ethical user terms
	4.	That OpenAI implement clearer, more visible consent prompts before publishing any user-generated content publicly

As an early childhood education professional and centre manager in Australia, I work within a legal and ethical framework that prioritises privacy, cultural safety, and responsible digital engagement. This includes the Education and Care Services National Law (WA) Act 2012, the National Quality Framework, and the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) — all of which demand high standards of ethical practice and accountability.

I am requesting a timely resolution to this matter. If I do not receive a satisfactory response, I will consider escalating this complaint to relevant data protection and consumer rights authorities, such as the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) and the eSafety Commissioner.

I am happy to provide further documentation or evidence of the content used without consent if needed.

Sincerely,
Western Australia
reviews.title: Privacy complaint and refund request – Sora default public sharing of user-generated content

reviews.content:
One of the most frustrating aspects of the game is its aggressive marketing strategy. Players often find themselves inundated with prompts to purchase boosters or extra lives every 2-4 levels, which can quickly disrupt the flow of the game.

This relentless push for in-game purchases feels excessive, especially for those just looking to enjoy a casual gaming experience. Instead of focusing solely on the enjoyment of matching candies and strategizing to clear levels, players are frequently bombarded with offers that detract from the overall experience. The game often seems to prioritize monetization over player engagement, leading to a sense of frustration.

Moreover, the user interface can be overwhelming, requiring multiple clicks just to navigate through the various prompts and start playing. This can make the game feel more like a chore than a leisurely pastime, as players are forced to sift through a barrage of notifications and advertisements before they can even get back to the challenging puzzles.

While Candy Crush undoubtedly has its merits in terms of design and gameplay mechanics, the over-the-top marketing tactics can significantly diminish the enjoyment for many players. Balancing engagement with monetization would greatly enhance the overall experience, allowing players to immerse themselves in the game without constant distractions.

Annoying!

reviews.content:
When I first downloaded CapCut a couple of years ago it was amazing. I can’t even remember if CapCut Pro was a thing back then but if it was, it clearly wasn’t as intrusive as it is today if I have no recollection of it. 

CapCut used to be a great app to make all sorts of videos on. It was easy to use and had a ton of brilliant features. It was the best free editing software around imo and I used it all the time. 

But slowly, CapCut Pro began to take precedent, and popular features, effects etc. began to disappear behind a paywall to the point where there’s really no point in calling it a “free” editing software anymore because so many of the features are behind its subscription service. 

I get it. Apps need to make money, but at this point CapCut is just another great thing that’s been ruined by corporate greed. This app is owned by the same company that owns TikTok, there’s no way they NEED CapCut to be as money grubbing as it is these days.

The app is virtually useless if you’re not able to pay, and the “free” version has been completely gutted (when they put smooth slow-mo behind a paywall I knew it was over for non-Pro users).

I’m done using CapCut. Going to try and find another free editing software that will likely fall to the same fate as CapCut. I hate it here. 

Giving the app 1 star because I’m too annoyed.
reviews.title: Deleted the App. I’m tired of Paywalls and Subscription Services.

reviews.content:
Temu is one of the most disappointing and misleading platforms I’ve ever used.
1.Product Quality Is Terrible
Items are often broken, missing parts, or look nothing like the pictures. You get what you pay for — and even that’s being generous.
2.Fake Discounts and Forced Ratings
It’s suspicious how Temu has a 4.6-star rating on the App Store when independent platforms like Reviews.io rate them as low as 1.5 stars. It’s likely they push users to leave a 5-star review to unlock “discounts” or prizes, manipulating their public image.
3.Sketchy Prize Spins = Gambling, Not Shopping
Every time you log in, you’re hit with a “Spin the Wheel” game. The first spin always lands on “Try Again,” and the second conveniently hits the jackpot — but you never actually get the prize unless you buy a bunch of random low-quality junk first. It’s deceptive and feels more like a gambling app than a shopping experience.
4.Misleading Promotions and Fake Urgency
The app constantly bombards you with emails titled “URGENT” or “ACTION REQUIRED” just to get your attention. This bypasses spam filters and tricks you into thinking something important is happening — it’s not. It’s just another fake promotion designed to get you to spend more.
5.Ethical and Legal Red Flags
•Multiple reports of intellectual property theft from small artists.
•Accusations of forced labor in their supply chain, including connections to Uyghur labor camps.
•Toxic and unsafe products reported, including children’s clothing with illegal levels of lead and antimony.
•Some users have even received disturbing items like a dog’s tooth necklace labeled as resin jewelry.
6.Manipulative Shopping Tactics
To get your “discount” or “prize,” you’re forced to buy a bunch of small, useless items. In the end, you spend way more than your original budget — all for something that should have been free or discounted to begin with.
7.Shady Customer Service
If something goes wrong (and it probably will), good luck. Responses are robotic, repetitive, and unhelpful. They rarely resolve anything properly.
Every part of this app is a trap — from fake urgency, trick-game mechanics, low-quality goods, to shady ethics. I’m shocked there hasn’t been a lawsuit yet for their deceptive advertising and bait-and-switch promotions.
If you’re even thinking about downloading Temu — don’t.

reviews.content:
Roblox can be a creative playground for kids, but parentsbe aware: multiple investigative reports and lawsuits have documented instances of grooming, sexualized content, and predatory behavior on the platform. These aren’t anonymous rumors major outlets and legal filings have raised serious concerns about how effectively Roblox prevents predators from contacting children. 

Roblox says it prioritizes child safety and has policies, human moderators, and automated tools (like Sentinel and other safety initiatives) to detect and remove abusive behavior. They’ve announced new measures recently, but critics and some investigators say problems persist and that enforcement hasn’t fully kept up with the scale of the platform. If you’re a parent, don’t take Roblox’s safety claims at face value use the parental tools. 

Community watchdogs and creators (for example, influencer investigators and well-known devs) have amplified these issues publicly, which is part of why the conversation has gotten so loud. That said, Roblox’s official Safety Center includes useful parental controls and reporting pathways enable them, set chat to strict/disabled for young kids, and consider supervising play.  

What I’d like to see Roblox do next: stronger age verification that can’t be trivially bypassed, faster human review of grooming reports, clearer transparency on moderation statistics, and easier parent controls by default (not buried in settings). Until then, I can’t recommend this as a standalone kids’ app — it’s great for creativity, but the safety tradeoffs are real. Play together, parents. Report everything. Be loud.
reviews.title: The Best Game For Full Grown Adults That Like Kids (Not in The Good Way)

I think about 1/3 of my comments end up being deleted by what I’m assuming is some kind of moderation system. While some of my comments affected have been confrontational I’ve never abused anyone or gone too far. And now I’m seeing my comments deleted even for saying “That is factually incorrect” and “I disagree”.

It’s been an extremely toxic experience because I’m a pretty mild person and the people who respond to me are often flaming and spreading misinformation, and it seems like the moment someone else takes things in a bad direction I end up getting my comments moderated, not them, probably because I’m using this App.

My comment:
“Search YouTube: Inside OpenAI Stargate
to see where you went wrong on how they use water”

So that’s an easy 1 star for this App, as I’m literally penalized and I guess used as a test subject, just for using this App to access YouTube.

EDIT: Rage inducing. For some reason it’s gone back and removed totally benign comments. This is totally unacceptable.

EDIT 2: Few weeks later. Can’t do it anymore. About 90% of my comments are censored. I can’t defend myself, I can’t speak my mind, I can’t even support people or be kind. I’m arbitrarily blocked not just from arguments but from everything. If this is what happens when AI run our lives count me out, and up until now I was a huge advocate. This is WRONG.
